messages:
maria_sales: Hey team — Acme Health POC needs private access to our hosted API from their prod VPC (cidr 10.20.0.0/16). They're doing cross-account and want a non-internet path. Can we confirm recommended pattern and the exact SG/route entries so I can send to their infra by EOD?

sam_solutions: Two options depending on long-term needs: 1) PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoint to our hosted API) — lowest friction for hosted API. 2) VPC peering / TGW to support Redwood Private or Dedicated pools in their network. Which are they asking for now?

maria_sales: For this POC they want PrivateLink to our hosted API. They may ask about Dedicated later.

devon_netops: OK. For PrivateLink we publish an interface service. Customer creates a VPCE in their account. Key things to call out: 
- Service name (we'll share the exact ARN/service name)
- VPCE type: Interface
- Subnets: recommend 2+ AZs
- VPCE security group: ALLOW inbound TCP 443 from customer CIDR 10.20.0.0/16
- DNS: enable private DNS so api.redwood-inference.internal resolves to VPCE ENIs

charlie_eng: Note on Dedicated pools: if they later want Dedicated in their VPC we need either peering/TGW or a different PrivateLink mapping (more config). For the POC stick with hosted via PrivateLink.

devon_netops: Sample AWS CLI the customer can run to create the endpoint:
```bash
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-0aaa111 --service-name com.amazonaws.us-west-2.vpce-svc-0abcdEXAMPLE --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --subnet-ids subnet-aaa subnet-bbb --security-group-ids sg-allow-vpce
```
Security group guidance: inbound tcp/443 from 10.20.0.0/16, outbound tcp/443 to 0.0.0.0/0.

maria_sales: Can we provide them a simple test they can run after VPCE creation and the exact SG rule lines to paste into their ticket?

sam_solutions: SG rules (copy/paste):
- Inbound: Type HTTPS, Protocol TCP, Port 443, Source 10.20.0.0/16
- Inbound (optional monitoring): Type HTTPS, Protocol TCP, Port 443, Source x.x.x.x/32
- Outbound: Type HTTPS, Protocol TCP, Port 443, Destination 0.0.0.0/0
Test (one-liner using --resolve to hit a VPCE IP):
```bash
curl -v --resolve "api.redwood-inference.internal:443:10.20.15.23" https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health -H 'Authorization: Bearer <POC_KEY>'
```
Replace IP with a VPCE ENI private IP from `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces` or from the console.

devon_netops: Also send them a short checklist: 
- Ensure VPC has DNS hostnames + DNS resolution enabled
- Create VPCE in at least two private subnets (AZs)
- Attach the SG with rules above
- Enable private DNS for the endpoint if they want to call api.redwood-inference.internal directly
- (Optional) Turn on VPC Flow Logs for troubleshooting

maria_sales: Great. Charlie, can you prepare the exact service ARN and a short firewall blurb for their security team? I'll include CLI, SG snippet, and checklist in the email.

charlie_eng: On it. I'll include the VPCE service ARN and also add a note about Dedicated pool caveats: if they later request Dedicated instances inside their network we'll require peering/TGW and a route for our Dedicated service CIDR (e.g., 10.246.0.0/16) plus a cross-account IAM role for provisioning. I'll attach that as an appendix.

redwood-deploy-bot: Created ticket INFRA-2764 for PrivateLink service ARN + docs. Assignee: charlie_eng. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INFRA-2764

maria_sales: Thanks everyone — I'll draft the note and send to Acme infra in ~30m.
